Fuzzing

  • It is a broader term than Bruteforcing.
  • Automated software testing technique.
  • Generating random values, patterns and other datatypes and feeding these data on the target application and seeing how the application reacts.
  • This data or payload is applied and the response given the application is analyzed to get a understanding of the application's architecture and workflow.
  • The data can itself be invalid or unexpected but whether the target application crashes or not or does something else is carefully analyzed for getting an idea for exploitation.
  • Below are some of reasons why fuzzing is done :-

    • Uncovering Hidden Vulnerabilities

    • Automating Security Testing

    • Strengthening Input Validation (for preventing SQL injections or cross-site-scripting (XSS) )

    • Improving Code Quality

Bruteforcing

  • Its more of a targeted approach than Fuzzing.
  • Multiple combinations or possibilities of a specific value is tested against the target machine.
